purpose: Acknowledge a discard without changing bytes.
Write one byte beyond the requested offset.
Accept a write exceeding the configured payload budget.
Lose the captured VMM state while retaining volume data.
Accept a handoff layout with the wrong volume size.
Accept a started VMM that omits a handed-off memory region.
Replace a successfully served source page with zeros.

Return zeros instead of volume bytes when the page source fails. Only a campaign whose faults take a source away mid-stream falls back at all, which is why this is the generated schedule's entry rather than the recorded scenario's.
Leave the source sealed or paused after an abandoned migration.
Give a handoff up after its first failed receive while the source still holds its pages. The swizzle campaign's separated links fail a first receive on every seed, so this is its entry.

Keep waiting on a listed source nothing can reach after its hold is over, a migration's source or a fork's parent's host. Only a source cut off while still listed leaves the hold as the one evidence, and no campaign draws that fault, so the two scenarios are its entry. Each fails alone.

Send a handoff's next receive while a host still reports an earlier one in flight. Only a receive whose caller hung up is in flight when a retry looks, and no campaign draws that fault, so the scenario is its entry.

Report every page of a handoff's set as the source's for the peer backing's whole life, which told a fork's child that pages it had published had no object. Only a destination checkpointed while its source still serves retires one of them, which is why this is that scenario's entry.

Report a page of a handoff's set as the source's while the volume names a checkpoint from before the handoff, which a hole always seems to be, so a page of zeros the destination published and retired is loaded as the source's own.

Ask the source for every page a destination loads, including one it published since the handoff, which answers with the version the guest wrote past. Only a destination whose arena gives back a page it published while its source still serves loads one.
Fault a destination's stream pages all at once, so the scheduler orders their slots, evictions and requests.
Forget that evicted private bytes exist in scratch storage. Only the buggified campaign evicts enough to spill, so this is the entry the per-site injection made detectable.
Leave a pager's spill file sparse instead of allocating its whole extent. Another writer then fills the filesystem, and the guest's next spill fails for want of space.
Give back a RAM copy the guest stored into, as though it still held its origin's bytes. The campaign's give-back checks every page the guest maps against what it wrote.
Lose loaded or copied data when creating a resident page.
Locate every member at the start of its part.
Reclaim the checkpoints the selected one still reads from.
Reclaim a kept checkpoint no fork was taken from, as if only pins protected anything.
Compact a parent's checkpoint into its child, which bills the child for the parent's page.
Accept a Starter's snapshot load request that names a key this package loads. Linux only, as root.
Leave the prepared directory and its sockets to this process instead of the placement's Owner. Linux only, as root.
Give the VMM host paths instead of the placement's Within. Linux only, as root.
Let a Starter prepare one launch twice. Linux only, as root.
Admit a memory session from a process other than the VMM its Starter reported. Linux only, as root.
Count a sparse spill file at what it holds rather than at its promise.
Take the filesystem's size as the host's room, ignoring what other writers hold.
Tell a cache over its share to stop at its share rather than one region below it.
Admit a cache write the write budget cannot afford.
Keep the write budget's reserves for the lowest priorities instead of the highest.
Count spill promises at what they hold when the promises do not fit, so the host reports ready.
Let the cache fill the disk to the floor, leaving another host on the filesystem no room to promise a VM's staging.
Judge whether promises fit the filesystem by the space other writers leave now, so a host waiting for them is refused.
Serve a page cache disk item that names another key.
Serve a page cache disk item without checking its checksum.
Write every read item of an evicted disk region again, past half a region.
Let fills take the disk region kept free for the second chance.
Give an evicted disk region back while a read is still in flight from it.
Write a closed disk region's table before its items are synced.
Have a closed pull free what it copied, as pulls held regions before.
Index the region that was open when the host stopped, which has no table, instead of giving it back.
Keep a page cache disk file that names another deployment, whose page identities may name other bytes.
Give back a disk region whose table is torn without scanning its items.
Go back to the host's own cache alone when a read of the list of caches fails, instead of keeping the last list read.
Keep the first list of caches read and ignore every later one.
Weigh the host's cache by the disk limiter's moving share instead of the disk it is given.
Refuse to start a host whose promises fit the filesystem but not the space another writer holds now.
Open the page cache's file without its lock, so two hosts on one node share one file.
Accept a cache directory on another filesystem than the scratch, which the one disk limiter does not measure.
Close a pulled VM's pull when its machine ends, so the checkpoint a stop publishes after that keeps nothing on the disk.
Take the code from the caches listed now, so a drain changes it and every stripe becomes a miss.
Drop the cache of a host pod that did not answer one survey from the list of caches.
Rebuild an envelope from stripes of another code whose length fits this one.
Give up when the first k stripes fail the envelope's check, instead of rebuilding from other sets of k to find the wrong one.
Look a stripe up in the disk's index under any code, so a page kept under another code is read and refused instead of missed.
Find a page's first item in the disk's index whatever index was asked for, as an index that holds one stripe a page.
Put stripe i on rank i alone, dropping the indices a list shorter than the code is wide has no rank for.
Keep a stripe the rebuild of its envelope found wrong, so it is read again until its region goes.
Place every window by the list of caches, ignoring the share the cluster cache is turned on for, so a host with others in its list keeps a pulled VM as stripes it cannot rebuild alone.
Mark a peer down when a dial failed because its own caller gave up.
Close the connection of a request over its peer's budget instead of answering BUSY on it.
Count every class of a peer's requests against one budget, so a stream at its budget makes faults busy.
Send each reply as soon as it is built rather than after the replies to the requests before it.
Give up on a peer that closes a hello unanswered instead of speaking version 1 to it.
Never close a connection that hears nothing, so a request over a partition waits until it heals.
Send bulk reads without the host's background budget, so a fault's reply waits behind all the stream's bytes.
Answer a cache request that names another cache, as a reused address would.
Queue a keep over the background budget instead of dropping it.
Send stripe reads without the bound on stripe bytes in flight.
Close a connection over a hello a duplicating link delivered twice, racing the dialer's first request.
Send stripe reads over the fault class, where a stripe waits behind every 2 MiB page reply ahead of it on its connection.
Serve stripes past the host's serving bandwidth instead of answering BUSY.
Hand back a raw page as a slice of its reply's pooled buffer, which the next reply is read into.
End a request's receive context before its payload is read, so a socket's read deadline fails every keep.
Fill the cluster with a part before its PUT has succeeded.
Take a keep for a window the cache's own list does not rank it for.
Fill in front of a read of the store: its callers wait for the right, the split and the keeps.
Fill from every read of the store, with no fill right asked of rank 1.
Wait for room in the queue of writes to the host's disk rather than drop the fill.
Queue a keep for stripes the cache is already writing rather than drop it.
Ask fill rights and send keeps on goroutines of their own, so the scheduler orders them on the link.
Take from each rank only the indices the list puts on it, which a change of ranks leaves few of (B5).
Ask every one of a window's first k+m ranks at once rather than k+1.
Ask a window's ranks in rank order, so every reader asks the same k+1 and the rest are never asked.
Never ask the rest of a window's ranks after the delay, so a read waits for its slowest holder.
Ask the rest of a window's ranks after the delay whatever the budget holds.
Leave a stripe a rebuild found wrong with its holder rather than telling it to drop it.
Read the store past the bound whatever the token bucket holds.
Count a holder that holds nothing of a window as one that timed out.
Mark down every host that times out, past a fifth of the list.
Probe a host marked down every second rather than after ten seconds growing to sixty.
Send fills to a host the reads have marked down.
Repair a rank with the index the list puts on it, whether or not another rank holds it.
Never check, by a HEAD, that the part behind a sampled hit still exists.
Hand each part of a publication to the fills as its PUT ends, so the scheduler orders a host's fills.
Write a publication's part to the hot tier before its regional PUT has succeeded.
Fail a read whose hot tier failed rather than read the regional bucket.
Give a store a hot tier beside a cache that fills the cluster.
Copy a missed object, or write a published one, to the hot tier in front of the read or the publication.
Hold every fill of the hot tier, whatever the queue's bound.
Drop the remembered survey only when a move begins, so a survey a host's read of the list of caches took during a start answers the command sent after it.
Report a fork's root as soon as its root publication installs, before it gives back its hold on the point it was forked at.
